Falling 1.03% to 7,341, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) marked its fourth day of consecutive losses, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) dropped 0.74% to 24,328 on technology sector weakness, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) tumbled 1.64% to 50,759.

Gold price dipped 0.18% to $3,849.20 as of U.S. market close, while the 10-Year Treasury yield edged down 3 basis points to 5.11% during a session in which energy stocks were the only real gainers, with financial services and healthcare stocks under the most pressure.

Today's biggest moves

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) plummeted 9.45% as security jitters and further AI replacement fears combined to punish software stocks. UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH) dropped 5.42% on sweeping anti-fraud proposals for Medicare & Medicaid. Crypto stocks, including Coinbase Global (NASDAQ:COIN) and Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD), tumbled as Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) continued its losing streak -- the leading crypto is now down over 20% in the past month.

What this means for investors

The recent string of technology outages that have hit air travel, banks, and other firms weighed further on stocks today, compounding (artificial intelligence) AI chip concerns and broader negative sentiment. Consumers are stockpiling essentials, which helped Costco Wholesale Corp (NASDAQ:COST)as Mizuho Securities just upped its price target on the stock.

Post-close earnings from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) beat analyst expectations, offering some reassurance on AI infrastructure demand and boosting peers in after-hours trading. Investors are still digesting the impact of new U.S. measures restricting international access to advanced AI chips, not only for Nvidia but for the whole sector.

title: Bill Ackman’s $14 billion bet beyond the Magnificent 7
detail:
Bill Ackman’s $14 billion bet beyond the Magnificent 7
Opeyemi Babalola
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 4:33 PM CST 4 min read
^GSPC
META
PS
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For three years, plenty of ordinary portfolios ran on seven engines. Anyone with an S&P 500 index fund leaned on the tech giants known as the Magnificent 7, whether they meant to or not.

That reliance got a rude reminder on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. The group lost more than $1 trillion in market value in one session, CNBC reported, on fears that the AI data center buildout could slow.

Bill Ackman had already been taking chips off that table. Pershing Square Inc. (PS), the firm he runs, sold about a third of its Microsoft (MSFT) shares in the third quarter, according to its latest 13F filing and the one before it. It also trimmed Meta Platforms (META) by roughly 11%, the filings show.

Also read: Billionaire Bill Ackman's market warning resurfaces as stocks plunge

The more telling number is what stayed.

Leaving aside its own firm and fund, Pershing held about $14 billion in stocks outside the Magnificent 7 on September 30, 2026, based on the latest filing. Those stakes make up nearly 70% of the portfolio.

Ackman trimmed Big Tech while it was rallying

The timing is the interesting part. Microsoft rallied hard in the quarter, so selling a third of the shares only shrank the position from about $2.3 billion to $2.1 billion, per the two filings. Meta's stake even grew in dollar terms.

That looks like housekeeping, not a verdict on Big Tech, and it came weeks before the November rout.

At Sept. 30 prices, the Microsoft shares sold were worth about $1.1 billion, based on the filings. Pershing's new Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) stake was worth about $1 billion, per the 13F.

Ackman effectively swapped a slice of Microsoft for the owner of the New York Stock Exchange.

ICE and Alcon are the newest names in the book

Neither appeared in the June filing, and the semiannual report of Pershing Square USA (PSUS), the firm's listed fund, says both were bought after June 30. Pershing called ICE a simple, predictable cash generator whose shares fell on worries it sees as unwarranted.

The second buy was Alcon (ALC), the Swiss maker of contact lenses and eye surgery gear. Pershing's stake was worth about $954 million at quarter-end, per the 13F.

The report argues that Alcon's roughly 20% operating margin sits well below its potential.

Netflix (NFLX) was the only existing holding Ackman added to. Pershing raised its stake by about 18% to 15.4 million shares, per the filings, even as the stock slipped.

The firm, which briefly owned Netflix in 2022, wrote that the company "has since effectively won the streaming wars."

title: Arista Networks (ANET) Is Quietly Breaking One of NVIDIA’s Biggest Advantages
detail:
Arista Networks (ANET) Is Quietly Breaking One of NVIDIA’s Biggest Advantages
Venkatesh Srinivasalu

ANET
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

We recently ranked the 10 Stocks to Buy as Investors Look Beyond NVIDIA, and Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) came in at number 7.

Arista Networks (ANET) Is Quietly Breaking One of NVIDIA's Biggest Advantages

For three years, the AI trade had one face. Now it has an interim CEO. On November 12, Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA's chief executive and board member, hours after nerves gripped investors awaiting the outcome of the board's crisis meeting. CFO Colette Kress is running the chipmaker on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. Analysts moved fast: Bernstein downgraded the stock to Market Perform and halved its target to $200, Baird cut it to Neutral, and Morgan Stanley dropped it from its Top Pick list.

The bigger question is cyclicality, not succession. At about 11x forward earnings, NVIDIA trades far below the S&P 500's roughly 19–20x, even after 106% revenue growth last quarter, a sign the market doubts those earnings will last. That is why money is spreading across the AI ecosystem: custom accelerators, the networking that ties clusters together, the clouds renting out compute, and the equipment that fills data halls.

Why Arista Made Our List

We built our list from U.S.-listed companies that sell alternatives to NVIDIA's products, from AI chips and networking to cloud services and data center equipment. To qualify, a company needed a market cap above $40 billion and Buy ratings from at least 70% of covering analysts. We then took the 10 largest and ranked them by median analyst upside.

Arista Networks, Inc. qualified because its Ethernet switches connect AI clusters built on any vendor's accelerators. With a market cap of $249 billion, Buy ratings from 100% of 33 analysts, and a median price target of $245 against a November 13 close of $197.29, the stock offers 24.18% upside, which placed it 7th on our list.

Arista Networks, Inc.: An NVIDIA Alternative

NVIDIA doesn't just sell chips; it sells the networking that connects them, and that bundle is a key part of its lock-in. Arista breaks that bundle. Its Ethernet switches work with any accelerator, so a customer mixing NVIDIA, AMD and custom chips can run them all on one open network.

That pitch is showing up in the numbers. On November 3, Arista reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5%, its fastest growth since going public. EPS of $1.20 beat the $1.08 estimate, and Q4 guidance of $3.9 billion to $4.0 billion came in above expectations. CEO Jayshree Ullal called it the company's highest growth since its IPO, with record profitability.

The risk is that NVIDIA fights back with its own Ethernet products, and that a handful of hyperscalers drive most of Arista's demand. Gross margin also dipped to 63.6% from 64.6%, a sign that competing for AI deals carries a cost.

title: Nike Is Down 78% From Its High. Here's What That Does to the Yield.
detail:
Nike Is Down 78% From Its High. Here's What That Does to the Yield.
Lawrence Rothman, CFA, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 4:50 PM CST 4 min read
NKE
^GSPC
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The overall market has done well over the last few years. Using the popular S&P 500 index as a proxy, large-cap stocks gained 61.5% over the last five years through Nov. 13.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

That's been positive for many, but certainly not all, stocks. Naturally, there have been laggards.

Nike (NYSE: NKE) has been one. The shares are about 78% off the high price during this period. Here's a look at the sell-off and the dividend yield to see whether or not you should buy the stock.

The stock's sell-off

This long-heralded company had big marketing budgets, famous commercials, multiple sports stars' endorsements, and growing sales. Investors did well by owning Nike's stock. However, over the last few years, a lack of product innovation, competition, and management missteps have led to sagging sales.

They don't look set to improve anytime soon, either. Nike's fiscal first-quarter revenue, adjusted to remove foreign-currency translations, dropped 5% year over year. The period ended on Aug. 31. Management forecasts revenue will fall by a high-single-digit percentage for the year.

With revenue persistently declining, it's no wonder the share price has dropped precipitously. Given the company's outlook, that doesn't look like it's going to reverse, at least not anytime soon.

Should the yield entice you?

Despite the company's struggles, Nike's board of directors has consistently raised dividends. In fact, the company has increased dividends annually for about a quarter of a century.

The lower stock price translates into a higher dividend yield. That's because you calculate a stock's yield by dividing the annual dividend by the share price. Hence, if a dividend stays constant or increases, the stock's yield rises.

Presently, Nike's shares yield 4.3%. That seems attractive, given that the S&P 500 yields 1.1%.

However, with weaker results, the company's operating cash flow has dropped over the past several years. Nike's fiscal 2026 operating cash flow fell from $3.7 billion to $2.9 billion. After subtracting $686 million for capital expenditures, it produced free cash flow (FCF) of $2.2 billion. This didn't cover the $2.4 billion of common and preferred stock dividends.

You can also look at dividends compared to earnings, called the payout ratio. Presently, Nike has a payout ratio of 79%.

Grab Holdings (NASDAQ:GRAB), a Southeast Asian super-app provider, closed at $3.18, down 0.93%, on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The decline was part of a broader U.S. stock market drop, as investors remained concerned about elevated inflation, rising interest rates, and growing government regulation toward the artificial intelligence sector. This week, the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released new restrictions meant to curb China's access to advanced AI chips.

Trading volume reached 101.8 million shares, coming in about 53% above its three-month average of 66.6 million shares. Grab Holdings IPO'd in 2020 and has fallen 73% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,341, down 1.03%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) ended at 24,328, down 0.74%. Among internet marketplaces and platform-based mobility, delivery, and fintech services, Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) closed at $68.81, down 1.69%, and DoorDash (NASDAQ:DASH) finished at $164.91, down 2.87%.

What this means for investors

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Grab's annual general meeting (AGM) notice for December 14 kept the stock in focus as investors watched for any updates on capital allocation. This is particularly noteworthy after the company's Nov. 9 announcement of a partnership with SoftBank Group to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure in Malaysia, expanding Grab's role in Southeast Asia's AI buildout.

The move raises Wall Street concerns over capex spending amid rising global fuel costs and how that would impact Grab's delivery business. That said, the company appears to be on a roll.

Two weeks ago, Grab reported third-quarter revenue rose 27% and raised 2026 guidance, which helped frame the stock's stronger fundamental backdrop. The company has also executed share buybacks, and committed to repurchasing $500 million worth of shares over the next 12 months, after already repurchasing $400 million across September and October of this year.

Earlier in 2026, Grab agreed to acquire a controlling 60% equity interest in Atome Financial, adding to its financial services push, and investors are watching whether that strategy lifts future earnings power.
